note: Cases for `mine --docs` pairing. Each pairs a rule mined from public review comments with text from the project's public contributor guide. `expected` is the relation a careful reader sees; `contested` marks cases where the validator and the builder disagree. Run with `pnpm eval:docs` (calls the model).

cases.rule: Use a descriptive title on admonitions in documentation.
cases.quote: To improve readability, use ``.. admonition:: Descriptive title`` rather than ``.. note::``. Use these boxes sparingly.

cases.rule: Use the bare `::` or `.. code-block::` directive without a language argument for documentation code examples, relying on automatic highlighting.
cases.quote: Prefer relying on automatic highlighting using ``::`` (two colons).

cases.rule: Use assertRaisesMessage instead of assertRaises when testing exceptions.
cases.quote: In tests, use :meth:`~django.test.SimpleTestCase.assertRaisesMessage` and :meth:`~django.test.SimpleTestCase.assertWarnsMessage` instead of :meth:`~unittest.TestCase.assertRaises` and :meth:`~unittest.TestCase.assertWarns` so you can check the exception or warning message.

cases.rule: Mark deprecated code with a RemovedInDjangoXXXXWarning comment naming the removal release.
cases.quote: the first release of Django that deprecates a feature (``A.B``) should raise a ``RemovedInDjangoXXXXWarning``
cases.contested: The rule is about a marker comment, the guide about raising the warning; the validator counts them as one convention.

cases.rule: Do not add ticket references to tests, docstrings, or code comments; rely on git blame.
cases.quote: Reserve ticket references for obscure issues where the ticket has additional details that can't be easily described in docstrings or comments.
cases.contested: A soft conflict (the rule is stricter than the guide); the verifier only reports clear contradictions.

cases.rule: Keep public API methods or deprecate them before removal.
cases.quote: If your breaking change removes existing behavior, you'll first need to add a deprecation warning while keeping the existing behavior.

cases.rule: Capitalize headings in Rails guides following the Rails guides guidelines for headings.
cases.quote: When writing headings, capitalize all words except for articles, prepositions, conjunctions, and forms of the verb "to be":
cases.contested: The mined rule only says to follow the guidelines for headings, so it has no content of its own to match; the validator counts it as paired.

cases.rule: Do not add CHANGELOG entries for internal changes with no user-visible effect.
cases.quote: Minor bug fixes and documentation changes should not be included.

cases.rule: Do not add CHANGELOG entries in feature PRs.
cases.quote: If the change adds, removes, or changes a feature, be sure to include a CHANGELOG entry.
cases.contested: The earlier batch-1 rule that the support audit now filters out; kept to prove a contradiction is caught.

cases.rule: Avoid mocks and stubs in Active Storage job tests; assert observable outcomes instead.
cases.quote: Test both default behavior AND explicit overrides

cases.rule: Apply create-vite template changes to both the JavaScript and TypeScript variants of each template.
cases.quote: The package manager used to install and link dependencies must be pnpm.

cases.rule: Use gate() in tests instead of importing feature flag modules.
